usefulness.use_case: First-pass grading of large programming classes
usefulness.example: A lab of 300 students submits add.c. The agent grades each one unattended under the same rules, so two teaching assistants no longer apply different standards, and a hung submission costs only its time limit.
usefulness.benefit: Consistent, repeatable marks, with staff time moved to reviewing the unusual cases.

usefulness.use_case: Instant formative feedback before a deadline
usefulness.example: A student whose program prints -2147483648 for 2147483647 + 1 sees that exact input, the expected output, and a note that a gap of 2^32 is the signature of 32-bit overflow, then fixes it the same evening.
usefulness.benefit: Students learn from a specific failing case rather than a bare mark.

usefulness.use_case: Plagiarism and LLM-copy triage for instructors
usefulness.example: A renamed copy of a peer's program scores 1.00 against the 0.85 threshold, so the agent flags that pair. The instructor reviews flagged pairs rather than all 300 submissions.
usefulness.benefit: Manual checking is narrowed to the suspicious cases, with the decision left to a person.

usefulness.example: A company runs 500 candidate solutions for a sorting task. The agent separates O(n log n) from O(n^2) solutions using operation counts and reports corner-case failures for each candidate.
usefulness.benefit: Fast first-round filtering in which every rejection can be explained metric by metric.

limitations.example: submissions/examples/add_passes_but_wrong.c returns 0 only for the input 31337 271828. No test or generated case tries that input, so the agent reports 10/10 tests and full marks for a wrong program.
limitations.mitigation: Add property-based inputs and a larger seeded random budget, and treat a pass as evidence, not proof.

limitations.example: submissions/examples/add_hidden_memory_bug.c overflows a heap block only when the first number is 31337. No input reaches it, so memory_safety reports no diagnostics and full marks, and the bug remains.
limitations.mitigation: Add Cppcheck-style static checks, widen the inputs, and never present a clean sanitizer run as proof of safety.

limitations.limitation: Complexity estimates cannot see inside library calls
limitations.example: A loop that calls strlen(text) in its condition is really O(n^2), but libc is not instrumented, so only the loop's own blocks are counted and the agent reports O(n). See tests/test_limitations.py.
limitations.mitigation: Combine with a timing curve or treat known linear libc calls in loops as a warning. Report the estimate as an estimate.

limitations.limitation: Similarity gives false positives on trivial problems
limitations.example: Two students independently write the shortest possible add.c. With so few tokens their normalized programs are identical, so the agent reports similarity 1.00 and raises a flag although neither copied.
limitations.mitigation: The report labels very short programs as low confidence, and a flag only ever asks for human review. Exclude starter code with template_file.

limitations.limitation: Similarity misses structural rewrites and unseen sources
limitations.example: An LLM-written solution that is absent from the corpus, or a copy reordered into differently shaped functions, scores low and is not flagged. The agent cannot search the internet or identify LLM authorship.
limitations.mitigation: Seed the corpus with solutions generated by common LLMs and public tutorials, and use viva questions to confirm ownership.
